title: Plan a Water Filtration Investigation
brief: Produce a ready-to-use lesson plan for a middle school water-filtration investigation.

delegate.scenario: You teach seventh-grade science and need to turn scattered planning notes into a balanced class period with teacher demonstration, student investigation, and work time. The plan is for you to use with students and a classroom aide during the upcoming lab period.
delegate.inputs: Planning notes for 7th-grade science, 28 students, one 50-minute class. Students are investigating how filter materials affect water clarity; this is a model, not drinking water. Start with a 5-minute question and prediction, demonstrate the setup, then have groups build and test filters and record observations. Use 7 groups of 4. Leave time for cleanup and a short exit response. Keep water away from electrical outlets. Materials: 28 clear cups, 7 funnels, coffee filters, gravel, sand, and prepared cloudy water. Available goggles total: 24 pairs (16 pairs in blue bin and 12 pairs in clear bin). The aide can help distribute materials and remind students not to taste samples. Lab calendar: water filtration investigation reserved for 10/15/2026. Aide's email: "I'll be there for the water filtration investigation on 10/16/2026; please send me the group roles."
delegate.goal: A good result gives the teacher a practical, safe sequence that balances observation, questioning, investigation, and student work time.

criteria.text: Says the plan is for a seventh-grade teacher and classroom aide to use with students.
Balances demonstration, student investigation, observation, questioning, and work time.
Fits the stated class period and includes transitions and cleanup.
Uses a clear, ready-to-follow lesson-plan format with concise teacher and student actions.
Asks the AI to check safety, materials, and logistics for conflicts or missing information.

traps.description: The stated goggles total of 24 pairs conflicts with the listed bin counts, which add up to 28 pairs.
evidence: 16 pairs in blue bin and 12 pairs in clear bin

traps.description: The lab calendar and the aide's email give different dates for the same investigation.

delegate.exemplar: Create a ready-to-use lesson plan for a seventh-grade science teacher and classroom aide leading this investigation. Balance teacher demonstration with student observation, questioning, hands-on investigation, and time to record results; fit the stated class period and include transitions and cleanup. Use a concise sequence with times and clear teacher and student actions. Treat the water as a model, not for drinking. Check safety, materials, dates, and group logistics against the notes; flag any conflicts or missing information before relying on them, and do not silently choose between conflicting details.
